technical.summary: CMI shows short-term bullish momentum with golden cross and stochastic confirmation, but lacks intermediate/long-term trend alignment and weak ADX suggests caution on trend strength.

fundamental.summary: CMI shows no actionable smart money signals with zero insider activity, no institutional positioning data, absent government contracts, no lobbying activity, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 81 days present timing risk.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (VIX-equivalent score 12) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but stale congressional data (2+ years old) and absent news sentiment provide no confirmation.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds with VIX in crisis territory (415.5), flat yield curve signalling recession risk, and strong USD headwind for industrials multinational exposure; CPI event already passed but macro stress remains acute.

debate.key_bull_argument: Short-term technical momentum (EMA 9/21 golden cross, stochastic bullish cross, supertrend bullish) with extreme fear sentiment (VIX crisis) creates contrarian buy opportunity near support level 178.35.
debate.key_bear_argument: Fundamental score of 2, zero smart money conviction, price below both 50/200 EMAs, weak ADX trend confirmation, and severe macro headwinds (VIX crisis, flat yield curve, strong USD) overwhelm short-term technicals and create unacceptable risk/reward.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term technicals (EMA 9/21 golden cross, stochastic bullish) offer entry at support, but fundamental vacuum (score 2), zero smart money conviction, and severe macro headwinds (VIX crisis, flat yield curve, strong USD) create unacceptable risk/reward asymmetry.
decision.primary_risk: Macro environment in crisis mode (VIX 415.5, recession-signal yield curve) will likely override short-term technicals; price below 50/200 EMAs leaves no intermediate trend support if momentum fails.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case dominance
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding CMI with 27 existing Industrials positions (14% of portfolio); concentration risk and sector saturation argue against adding exposure.
